<h1>Eigen-Decomposition & DMD: State-Space & Modal Identification</h1>
<p class="hero-lead">
Transform second-order mechanics into continuous first-order <span class="highlight-blue">state-space models</span> $\dot{\mathbf{z}} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{z}$. 
Extract coherent spatiotemporal modes directly from experimental sensor measurement snapshots using the 
<span class="highlight-orange">Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD)</span> algorithm.
</p>
</div>

<ul style="margin: 0; padding-left: 20px;">

<li><strong>Map</strong> complex eigenvalues $\lambda = \sigma \pm i \omega_d$ onto decay rates and damped oscillation frequencies.</li>
<li><strong>Construct</strong> time-shifted measurement snapshot data matrices $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{X}'$.</li>

<!-- Section 2: Theory -->
<section class="lesson-section" id="sec-theory">
<div class="section-header">
<div class="section-tag">01 · State-Space Mechanics</div>
<h2>4.1 Continuous State-Space Representation</h2>
<p>Defining the state vector $\mathbf{z}(t) = [\mathbf{x}(t)^T, \dot{\mathbf{x}}(t)^T]^T \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$:</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<div class="eq-box">
$$\dot{\mathbf{z}}(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \dot{\mathbf{x}} \\ \ddot{\mathbf{x}} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{0} & \mathbf{I} \\ -\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{K} & -\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{C} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{x} \\ \dot{\mathbf{x}} \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{A} \mathbf{z}(t)$$
</div>

<p>
The complex eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$, denoted $\lambda_j = \sigma_j \pm i \omega_{d,j}$, directly determine:
</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Stability / Decay Rate:</strong> $\sigma_j = \operatorname{Re}(\lambda_j) < 0$ guarantees asymptotic stability.</li>
<li><strong>Damped Oscillation Frequency:</strong> $\omega_{d,j} = |\operatorname{Im}(\lambda_j)|$.</li>
<li><strong>Modal Damping Ratio:</strong> $\zeta_j = -\sigma_j / \sqrt{\sigma_j^2 + \omega_{d,j}^2}$.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>

<!-- Section 3: DMD -->
<section class="lesson-section" id="sec-dmd">
<div class="section-header">
<div class="section-tag">02 · Data-Driven Algorithms</div>
<h2>4.2 Exact Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD)</h2>
<p>Given sensor measurement snapshots sampled at uniform time step $\Delta t$, assemble two data matrices:</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<div class="eq-box">
$$\mathbf{X} = [\mathbf{z}_1, \mathbf{z}_2, \dots, \mathbf{z}_{m-1}], \quad \mathbf{X}' = [\mathbf{z}_2, \mathbf{z}_3, \dots, \mathbf{z}_m]$$
</div>

<p>DMD discovers the best-fit linear operator $\mathbf{A}$ advancing snapshots forward in time ($\mathbf{X}' \approx \mathbf{A} \mathbf{X}$) via low-rank Truncated SVD:</p>

<div class="eq-box">
$$\mathbf{X} \approx \mathbf{U}_r \mathbf{\Sigma}_r \mathbf{V}_r^* \quad \implies \quad \tilde{\mathbf{A}} = \mathbf{U}_r^* \mathbf{X}' \mathbf{V}_r \mathbf{\Sigma}_r^{-1}$$
</div>

<p>
Computing eigenvectors $\mathbf{w}_j$ of reduced matrix $\tilde{\mathbf{A}}$ yields exact full-state dynamic modes:
</p>

<div class="eq-box">
$$\mathbf{\Phi}_j = \mathbf{X}' \mathbf{V}_r \mathbf{\Sigma}_r^{-1} \mathbf{w}_j, \quad \lambda_j = \frac{\ln(\mu_j)}{\Delta t}$$
</div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- Section 4: Misconceptions -->
<section class="lesson-section" id="sec-misconceptions">
<div class="callout-important">
<div class="callout-title">
<svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"><path d="M10.29 3.86L1.82 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.71 3h16.94a2 2 0 0 0 1.71-3L13.71 3.86a2 2 0 0 0-3.42 0z"/><line x1="12" y1="9" x2="12" y2="13"/><line x1="12" y1="17" x2="12.01" y2="17"/></svg>
Common Misconception · Is DMD Merely Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD / PCA)?
</div>
<p style="margin: 0 0 8px 0;">
No. POD / PCA decomposes measurement fields into orthogonal spatial modes based purely on variance, but mixes multiple temporal frequencies together.
</p>
<p style="margin: 0;">
<strong>DMD modes oscillate at a single, distinct complex frequency and exponential decay rate.</strong> DMD combines spatial dimensionality reduction with discrete Fourier time-stepping, allowing engineers to isolate which physical structure vibrates at a specific frequency $\omega_j$.
</p>
</div>
</section>

<!-- Section 5: Quiz -->
<section class="lesson-section" id="sec-quiz">
<div class="section-header">
<div class="section-tag">03 · Diagnostic Checkpoint</div>
<h2>4.3 Check Your Understanding</h2>
<p>Test your understanding of DMD eigenvalue mapping.</p>
</div>

<div class="quiz-box">
<div class="quiz-question">
<strong>Question:</strong> If an exact DMD discrete eigenvalue is computed as $\mu_j = 0.98 \exp(i 0.25)$ with sampling interval $\Delta t = 0.01\text{ s}$, what are the continuous decay rate $\sigma_j$ and oscillation frequency $\omega_j$?
</div>
<div class="quiz-options">
<div class="quiz-opt" data-correct="true" data-explanation="Continuous eigenvalue lambda = ln(mu) / dt = [ln(0.98) + i * 0.25] / 0.01 = [-0.0202 + i * 0.25] / 0.01 = -2.02 + 25.0i. Thus sigma = -2.02 1/s (stable decay) and omega = 25.0 rad/s!">
A. $\sigma_j = -2.02\text{ s}^{-1}$ (exponential decay), $\omega_j = 25.0\text{ rad/s}$.
</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" data-correct="false" data-explanation="Remember continuous lambda = ln(mu)/dt, not mu/dt!">
B. $\sigma_j = +0.98\text{ s}^{-1}$, $\omega_j = 0.25\text{ rad/s}$.
</div>
<div class="quiz-opt" data-correct="false" data-explanation="Since |mu| = 0.98 < 1, the continuous real part ln(|mu|)/dt must be negative (decaying, stable), not positive!">
C. $\sigma_j = +2.02\text{ s}^{-1}$ (explosive instability), $\omega_j = 250.0\text{ rad/s}$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="quiz-feedback"></div>
</div>
</section>

<!-- Section 6: Code -->
<section class="lesson-section" id="sec-code">
<div class="section-header">
<div class="section-tag">04 · Computational Implementation</div>
<h2>4.4 SVD-Based DMD in Python</h2>
<p>Extract dynamic modes and eigenvalues from measured snapshot matrices.</p>
</div>

<div class="code-box">
<div class="code-header">
<div class="code-tabs">
<button class="code-tab-btn active">Python (NumPy / SVD)</button>
</div>
<button class="btn-copy">Copy Code</button>
</div>
<pre class="code-block"><code>import numpy as np

def compute_exact_dmd(X, X_prime, rank=4, dt=0.01):
    # Step 1: Truncated SVD of X
    U, s, Vh = np.linalg.svd(X, full_matrices=False)
    Ur = U[:, :rank]
    Sr = np.diag(s[:rank])
    Vr = Vh[:rank, :].conj().T

    # Step 2: Low-rank projection of linear operator A
    Atilde = Ur.conj().T @ X_prime @ Vr @ np.linalg.inv(Sr)

    # Step 3: Spectral decomposition of Atilde
    eigenvalues, W = np.linalg.eig(Atilde)

    # Step 4: Full DMD Modes Phi
    Phi = X_prime @ Vr @ np.linalg.inv(Sr) @ W

    # Continuous time eigenvalues
    omega_continuous = np.log(eigenvalues) / dt
    return Phi, eigenvalues, omega_continuous</code></pre>
</div>
</section>
